en: Relating to the circulatory system, that is the heart and blood vessels.

cardiovascular.ety:

From cardio- + vascular.

ex.en: Lungs, heart, veins, arteries and capillaries form the cardiovascular system.
ex.ja: 肺、心臓、静脈、動脈、毛細血管により循環器系が形成されています。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kardia（心臓）+ ラテン語 vasculum（小さな管）。「心臓血管の」。cardiac と同じ。

en: Elegant, stylish.
Good form; style.
A person with (a particular type of) chic.

chic.ety: Borrowed from French chic (“elegant”), which in turn is probably borrowed from German Schick (“elegant appearance; tasteful presentation”). The word is akin to Dutch schielijk (“hasty”), schikken (“to arrange”) and Old English sċēon (“to happen”).

note.ja: フランス語 chic（粋な）から。「シックな・あか抜けた」。

en: A living organism (originally a plant) produced asexually from a single ancestor, to which it is genetically identical.
A group of identical cells derived from a single cell.
To create a clone of.

clone.ety: Coined (in botany) in 1903, based on Ancient Greek κλών (klṓn, “twig”). Figurative use from the 1970s.

ex.en: At the ethics committee, a temporary halt to cloning experiments was decided.
ex.ja: 倫理委員会では, クローン実験の一時停止が決定した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 klōn（小枝・挿し木）から。挿し木で同じ植物を増やすことから「クローン」。

en: Pertaining to a community or a commune.
Shared by a community; public.

Borrowed from French communal, from Late Latin commūnālis, from Latin commūnis. Doublet of cominal.

ex.en: There is a communal kitchen in the dormitory.
ex.ja: 寮には共用のキッチンがある。

note.ja: com（共に）+ mun（務め）+ al。皆で共有する →「共同の・共有の」。

en: An association or combination of businesses, financial institutions, or investors, for the purpose of engaging in a joint venture.
A similar arrangement among non-commercial institutions or organizations.

note.ja: ラテン語 consortium（運命を共にすること）から。con + sors（運命・分け前）。「共同事業体」。consort（仲間）と同じ。

en: A count backward in fixed units to the time of some event, especially the launch of a space vehicle.
The acts of preparation carried out during this period.

ex.en: The countdown has begun.
ex.ja: カウントダウンが始まりました。

ex.en: The countdown to the conquest of every sentence has finally begun.
ex.ja: ついに全文制覇へのカウントダウンが始まってしまった。

note.ja: count（数える）+ down（下へ）。「数を減らしながら数えること」→「秒読み」。

en: A person who delivers messages.
A company that delivers messages.
To deliver by courier.

courier.ety: From a convergence of Middle English corour, currour, from Old French coreor, agent noun of corir (“to run”), and Middle English courier, a borrowing of Middle French courrier, from Italian corriere.

note.ja: ラテン語 currere（走る）から。cour（走る）+ ier。走る人 →「宅配業者・急使」。

en: Of the nature of a disaster; calamitous.
Foreboding disaster; ill-omened.

disastrous.ety: From disaster + -ous, after Middle French desastreux (modern French désastreux; from desastre (modern French désastre, “disaster”; from des- + astre, a calque of Italian disastro) + -eux), itself after Italian disastroso, from disastro + -oso, from dis- (“away, without”) (from Latin dis-) + astro (“star, planet”) (from Latin astrum (“star, celestial body”), from Ancient Greek ᾰ̓́στρον (ắstron)).

ex.en: Pollution has a disastrous effect on the ecology of a region.
ex.ja: 汚染公害は地域の生態環境に壊滅的な影響を与える。

note.ja: dis（悪い）+ astr（星）+ ous。悪い星の下にある（占星術から）→「悲惨な・壊滅的な」。disaster（災害）。

en: To die from suffocation while immersed in water or other fluid.
To kill by suffocating in water or another liquid.

drown.ety:
From Middle English drownen, drounen, drunen (“to drown”), of obscure and uncertain origin.
The OED suggests an unattested Old English form *drūnian. Harper 2001 points to Old English druncnian, ġedruncnian (> Middle English drunknen, dronknen (“to drown”)), "probably influenced" by Old Norse drukkna (cf. Icelandic drukkna, Danish drukne (“to drown”)). Funk & Wagnall's has 'of uncertain origin'. It has been theorised (see e.g. ODS) that it may represent a direct loan of Old Norse drukkna, but this is described by the OED as being "on phonetic and other grounds [...] highly improbable", unless

ex.en: I might as well drown as starve.
ex.ja: 飢え死にするくらいなら、溺れ死んだほうがましだ。

note.ja: 中英語 drounen から。北欧語に由来するとされる。drink と同じ祖先。「溺れる」。

en: One who plays the drums.
A drumstick (the lower part of a chicken or turkey leg).

drummer.ety: From drum + -er (occupational suffix) or + -er (relational noun suffix).

ex.en: The only drummer here is Tom.
ex.ja: ここにいるドラマーはトムだけだよ。

en: Able to resist wear or decay; lasting; enduring.
A durable thing, one useful over more than one period, especially a year.

durable.ety: From Middle English durable, from Old French durable, from Latin dūrābilis (“lasting, permanent”), from dūrō (“harden, make hard”).

ex.en: It seems durable enough.
ex.ja: これは耐久性に欠けているようです。

ex.en: Are printers a non-durable good?
ex.ja: プリンターは、消耗品ですか？

ex.en: These trousers are made of durable cloth.
ex.ja: このズボンは長もちする布地でできている。

note.ja: dur（続く）+ able。長く続くことができる →「耐久性のある・丈夫な」。

en: The ability to produce a desired effect under ideal testing conditions.
A degree of ability to produce a desired effect; effectiveness.

en: That has been described as greater than it actually is; abnormally increased or enlarged.

ex.en: The report exaggerated the capacity of the hall.
ex.ja: その報告ではホールの収容能力が誇張されていた。

ex.en: He exaggerated his experience.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の経験を誇張していった。

ex.en: You may depend upon it that the story is exaggerated.
ex.ja: その話はきっと大げさに伝えられているのだ。

note.ja: exaggerate（誇張する）+ -ed。ex（外へ）+ aggerare（積み上げる）、agger（盛り土）。「盛り上げすぎた」→「誇張された」。

en: The act of excluding or shutting out; removal from consideration or taking part.
An item not covered by an insurance policy.

exclusion.ety: From Middle English exclusion, exclusioun, from Old French [Term?] and Latin exclusiō, from exclūdō. By surface analysis, exclude + -sion.

ex.en: Demand the exclusion of the country from the U. N.
ex.ja: その国の国連からの除名を要求する。

ex.en: He worships money to exclusion of everything else.
ex.ja: 彼は他のものが目に入らないほどお金を崇拝している。

ex.en: His work occupies his mind to the exclusion of all else.
ex.ja: 彼は仕事の事で頭がいっぱいで他は何も頭に入らない。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ clus（閉じる）+ ion。外に閉め出すこと →「除外・排除」。

en: A citizen or local inhabitant of the Philippines, or descendant of such.
Specifically the male equivalent of Filipina.
Of or pertaining to the Philippines or its peoples, languages, and cultures.
Of or pertaining to Tagalog, the basis of the national language of the Philippines.

Filipino.ety: From Spanish filipino m, from Felipe + -ino, demonym to Spanish las Islas Filipinas (“The Philippine Islands (P.I.); The Philippines”), after Spanish El Rey Felipe II de España (“King Philip II of Spain”). The Spanish term formerly only referred to a male Philippine-born person of pure or majority Spanish descent, synonym to Spanish insular (“islander”) (plural insulares) in the Spanish Colonial Era of the Philippines, before it was applied as a nationality for every citizen of the Philippines from the First Philippine Republic during the Philippine Revolution.

ex.en: "Are you from Australia?" asked the Filipino.
ex.ja: 「オーストラリアからですか」とフィリピン人はたずねました。

ex.en: Are you a Filipino?
ex.ja: あなたはフィリピン人ですか。

note.ja: スペイン語 Filipino から。フィリピンはスペイン王フェリペ2世（Felipe）にちなむ国名。

en: Someone who sells their services to clients without a long-term employment contract.
A medieval mercenary.
Of or relating to a freelance; without a long-term employment contract.
To work as a freelance.
To produce or sell services as a freelance.

It changed to a figurative noun around the 1860s and was recognized as a verb in 1903 by authorities such as

ex.en: More and more people are working as freelance IT-engineers.
ex.ja: フリーランスのITエンジニアとして働く人も増えている。

ex.en: Tom used to be a freelance photographer.
ex.ja: トムは以前、フリーランスの写真家だった。

en: A colourless non-aged alcoholic liquor made by distilling fermented grains such as barley, corn, oats or rye with juniper berries; the ba…
Gin rummy.
To remove the seeds from cotton with a cotton gin.
To trap something in a gin.
If.

gin.ety: Abbreviation of geneva, alteration of Dutch genever (“juniper”) from Old French genevre (modern French genièvre), from Vulgar Latin ziniperus, from Latin iūniperus (“juniper”). Hence gin rummy (first attested 1941).

ex.en: Gin is not my friend.
ex.ja: ギンは僕の友達じゃない。

ex.en: What do you need to make gin and tonic?
ex.ja: ジントニックを作るには何がいるの？

ex.en: I'd like a gin and tonic.
ex.ja: ジン・トニックをください。

note.ja: オランダ語 genever（ネズの実）の短縮。ジュニパーベリーで香りをつけた酒。

en: The period of time immediately following a marriage.
A trip taken by a newly married couple during this period.
To have a honeymoon (a trip taken by a couple after wedding).

honeymoon.ety:
From earlier hony moone, originally denoting the period of time following a wedding, equivalent to honey + moon. The original reference was to affection waning like the moon, but later the sense became "the first month, or moon after marriage", which tends to be the sweetest.
Compare Middle Low German suckermânt (“honeymoon”, literally “sugar-month”), German Low German Hönnigweken (“honeymoon”, literally “honey-weeks”). The German Honigmond (literally “honey-moon”) is a calque of French lune de miel, itself a calque of the English term.

ex.en: Mr. and Mrs. West are on their honeymoon.
ex.ja: ウエスト夫妻は新婚旅行中です。

ex.en: The couple went off on their honeymoon.
ex.ja: 二人はハネムーンに出かけた。

ex.en: A honeymoon in Canada costs a lot of money.
ex.ja: カナダへの新婚旅行には多くの金が必要である。

note.ja: honey（蜜）+ moon（月）。「蜜のように甘い最初の1か月」→「新婚旅行」。

The initiation of combustion.

note.ja: ignite（点火する）+ -ion。ラテン語 ignis（火）。「点火・（車の）イグニッション」。

en: Rendered less effective.
inebriated, drunk.
A criminal charge for driving a vehicle while impaired.

ex.en: Heavy smoking impaired his health.
ex.ja: 彼はたばこの吸いすぎで体を壊した。

note.ja: impair（損なう）+ -ed。im（〜に）+ pejorare（悪くする）。「損なわれた・障がいのある」。

en: Of or pertaining to investigation or an investigation.
Inquisitive; curious.

investigative.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *-iHwósder.

From investigate + -ive.

en: A precious or semi-precious stone; gem, gemstone.
A valuable object used for personal ornamentation, especially one made of precious metals and stones; a piece of jewellery.
To bejewel; to decorate or bedeck with jewels or gems.

jewel.ety: From Middle English juel, jewel, juwel, jeuel, jowel, from Anglo-Norman juel, from Old French jouel, joel, joïel, hence French joyau, of uncertain origin. Perhaps based ultimately on Latin gaudium (“joy”), or on Latin iocus (“joke; jest”), or according to Pihan, from Arabic جَوْهَر (jawhar). Compare Medieval Latin jocale. Displaced native Old English māþm.

ex.en: She passed the jewel off as her own.
ex.ja: 彼女はその宝石を自分のものとして通した。

ex.en: He locked up his jewels in the safe.
ex.ja: 彼は鍵をかけて宝石を金庫にしまいこんだ。

ex.en: I sold the best jewel that I had.
ex.ja: 私は持っているうちで一番良い宝石を売った。

note.ja: 古フランス語 jouel から。ラテン語 jocus（遊び・楽しみ）とされる。「宝石」。

en: A class of planets that are similar in mass to Jupiter.

jupiter.ety: Decapitalization, from planet Jupiter. From being a planet like Jupiter.

ex.en: Jupiter is the biggest planet in our solar system.
ex.ja: 木星は太陽系で最も大きな惑星です。

ex.en: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System.
ex.ja: 木星は、太陽系最大の惑星である。

ex.en: Jupiter is a big planet, right?
ex.ja: 木星は大きい惑星ですね。

note.ja: ローマ神話の最高神ユピテル（Jupiter）から。「木星」。

en: Evident to the senses, especially to the sight; apparent; distinctly perceived.
Obvious to the understanding; apparent to the mind; easily apprehensible; plain; not obscure or hidden.
A list or invoice of the passengers or goods being carried by a commercial vehicle or ship.
A file containing metadata describing other files.
To show plainly; to make to appear distinctly, usually to the mind; to put beyond question or doubt; to display; to exhibit.
To become manifest; to be revealed.

manifest.ety: From Middle English manifest, manifeste, from Latin manifestus, manufestus (“palpable, manifest”), from Latin manus (“hand”) + an uncertain second element. Doublet of manifesto.

ex.en: He manifested his character in his behavior.
ex.ja: 彼は振る舞いで性格を明らかに示した。

ex.en: He doesn't manifest much desire to win the game.
ex.ja: 彼は試合に勝ちたいという熱望を明らかに示さない。

ex.en: The mayor manifested his discontent with the new plan.
ex.ja: 市長は新計画に不満を表明した。

note.ja: ラテン語 manifestus（手で触れられるほど明らかな）から。manus（手）。「明らかな・はっきり示す」。manifesto も同じ。

en: In the same way, each to the other; reciprocally.
In a shared manner; equally; affecting all parties the same way.

mutually.ety:

From mutual + -ly.

ex.en: They mutually discussed the future.
ex.ja: 彼らはお互いに未来のことについて話し合った。

ex.en: These facts are mutually related.
ex.ja: この事実はお互いに関連し合っている。

ex.en: The two qualities are mutually exclusive.
ex.ja: その２つの性質は相容れない。

note.ja: mutual（相互の）+ -ly。ラテン語 mutuus（交換された）、mutare（変える）。「互いに」。

en: To plan, control and record the position and course of a vehicle, ship, aircraft, etc., on a journey; to follow a planned course.
To give directions, as from a map, to someone driving a vehicle.

navigate.ety: First attested in 1588; borrowed from Latin nāvigātus, the perfect passive participle of nāvigō (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from nāvis (“ship”) + -igō, from Proto-Indo-European *néh₂us (“boat”).

en: Extremely overweight, especially: weighing more than 20% (for men) or 25% (for women) over their conventionally ideal weight determined b…
A person who is obese.

obese.ety: From Latin obēsus, derived from obedō (“to devour, eat away”), from ob (“away”) + edō (“to eat”).

note.ja: ラテン語 obesus（食べて太った）から。ob + edere（食べる）。obesity と同じ。

en: The act of reaching out.
The act of raising awareness.
To reach further than.
To surpass or exceed.

From out- + reach.

en: A vista or point that gives a view down toward something else.
To offer a view (of something) from a higher position.
To fail to notice; to look over and beyond (anything) without seeing it.

overlook.ety:
Inherited from Middle English overloken.
From Middle English overloken; equivalent to over- + look.

ex.en: This kind of mistake is easy to overlook.
ex.ja: この種の間違いは見逃しやすい。

ex.en: These kinds of mistakes are easy to overlook.
ex.ja: この種の間違いは見逃しやすい。

ex.en: I liked the room overlooking the valley.
ex.ja: 私は谷間を見下ろす部屋が好きだった。

en: Of a disease: epidemic over a wide geographical area and affecting a large proportion of the population; also, of or pertaining to a dise…
A pandemic disease; a disease that affects a wide geographical area and a large proportion of the population.
The COVID-19 pandemic.

pandemic.ety: From Ancient Greek πάνδημος (pándēmos, “of or belonging to all the people, public”) + English -ic (suffix forming adjectives from nouns with the sense ‘of or pertaining to’). πάνδημος is derived from παν- (pan-, prefix meaning ‘all, every’) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to protect, shepherd”)) + δῆμος (dêmos, “the common people; free citizens, sovereign people”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *deh₂- (“to divide, share”)). Compare Late Latin pandēmus (“affecting all the people, general, public”).

ex.en: What is a pandemic?
ex.ja: パンデミックって何？

ex.en: What's the difference between an epidemic and a pandemic?
ex.ja: エピデミックとパンデミックって、何が違うの？

note.ja: pan（すべての）+ dem（民衆）+ ic。すべての人々に広がる →「世界的大流行（の）」。epidemic（民衆の間の流行）より範囲が広い。

en: The sum of the distance of all the lengths of the sides of an object.
The length of such a boundary.

perimeter.ety: From Latin perimetros, Ancient Greek περίμετρος (perímetros). Equivalent to peri- + meter.

en: A very long spear used two-handed by infantry soldiers for thrusting (not throwing), both for attacks on enemy foot soldiers and as a cou…
A sharp, pointed staff or implement.
To prod, attack, or injure someone with a pike.
To assume a pike position.

pike.ety:
From Middle English pyke, pyk, pik, pike (“pike; sharp point, iron tip of a staff or spear, pointed toe of an item of footwear; sharp tool; mountain, peak”), from Old English pīc (“pointed object, pick axe”), and Middle French pique (“long thrusting weapon”), from Old French pic (“sharp point, spike”); both ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *pīk, from Proto-Germanic *pīkaz, *pīkō (“sharp point, pike, peak”), related to pick with a narrower meaning.
The word is cognate with Middle Dutch pecke, peke, picke (modern Dutch piek), German Pike, Norwegian pik, Danish pig, and possibly Old Irish pīk.

note.ja: 古英語 pīc（とがったもの）から。「槍」→ 口のとがった魚 →「カワカマス」。peak、pick と同系。

en: Someone who preaches a worldview, philosophy, or religion, especially someone who preaches the gospel and especially a clergyman or clerg…

preacher.ety:
From Middle English precher, prechere; partly equivalent to preach + -er, and partly continuing Middle English prechour, prechiour, from Old French preecheor (French prêcheur), from Latin praedicator (“public praiser, proclaimer”). See preach.
Displaced native Old English bydel.

ex.en: Bob became a preacher.
ex.ja: ボブは牧師になりました。

en: To go before, go in front of.
To cause to be preceded; to preface; to introduce.
Brief editorial preface (usually to an article or essay).

precede.ety: From Middle French précéder, from Latin praecēdō, from prae- + cēdō.

ex.en: A rich life is always preceded by disaster.
ex.ja: 壊滅そのものが豊かな生命を生む。

ex.en: The rain was preceded by wind.
ex.ja: 雨になる前に風が吹いた。

ex.en: Your reputation precedes you.
ex.ja: お噂はかねがね伺っております。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ ced（行く）+ e。前に行く →「先立つ・先行する」。precedent（前例）。

en: The purchasing department of a company.
The act of procuring or obtaining; obtainment; attainment.

procurement.ety: Inherited from Middle English procurement, from Old French procurement, from procurer.

ex.en: We are trying to clarify your future procurement requirements.
ex.ja: お客様の今後の購買需要を明らかにしようとしています。

note.ja: procure（調達する）+ -ment。pro（代わりに）+ curare（世話をする）。「世話をして手に入れること」→「調達」。cure と同じ cur。

en: Someone who protects or guards, by assignment or on their own initiative.
A headmate who primarily fronts, or otherwise protects the system, in situations where the system is at risk of psychological harm.

protector.ety: From Middle English protectour, from Anglo-Norman protectour, protector and its etymon Latin prōtēctor, from prōtegō (“shield, protect”). By surface analysis, protect + -or. Displaced native Old English sċildend.

ex.en: Is there a protector on the part that is spinning?
ex.ja: 回っている部分にプロテクターはあるか？

en: A mixture of wood, cellulose and/or rags and water ground up to make paper.
A mass of chemically processed wood fibres (cellulose).
To make or be made into pulp.
To deprive of pulp; to separate the pulp from.
Of or pertaining to pulp magazines; in the style of a pulp magazine or the material printed within such a publication.

pulp.ety: From Middle English pulpe, from Latin pulpa.

ex.en: They beat the dog to a pulp.
ex.ja: 彼らはその犬をめったうちにした。

ex.en: Reduce to pulp by boiling.
ex.ja: くたくたに煮る。

note.ja: ラテン語 pulpa（果肉）から。「果肉・パルプ」→ 安いパルプ紙の雑誌 →「低俗小説」。

en: Money paid for the freeing of a hostage.
The release of a captive, or of captured property, by payment of a consideration.
To pay a price to set someone free from captivity or punishment.
To exact a ransom (payment) in exchange for the freedom of.

ex.en: The hijacker demanded a ransom of two million dollars.
ex.ja: 乗っ取り犯人は２００万ドルの身の代金を要求した。

note.ja: 古フランス語 rançon（買い戻し）から。ラテン語 redemptio。redemption と同じ語源。「身代金」。

en: A shaky or unsteady gait.
A lively dance originating in Scotland.
To wind on a reel.
To spin or revolve repeatedly.

reel.ety: From Middle English reel, reele, from Old English rēol, hrēol, from Proto-West Germanic *hrehul, from Proto-Germanic *hrehulaz, *hrahilaz, from Proto-Indo-European *krek- (“to weave, beat”). Cognate with Icelandic ræl, hræll.

ex.en: He reeled in a huge fish yesterday.
ex.ja: 昨日彼は大きな魚を釣り上げました。

ex.en: My punch sent him reeling into the rope.
ex.ja: 私のパンチは彼をロープに追い込んだ。

ex.en: My punch sent him reeling.
ex.ja: 私のパンチで彼はよろめいた。

note.ja: 古英語 hrēol（糸巻き）から。「リール」→ 糸巻きのようにくるくる回る →「よろめく」。

en: The practising of something which is to be performed before an audience, usually to test or improve the interaction between several parti…
A preparatory activity analogous to a rehearsal (sense 1).

rehearsal.ety: From Middle English rehercel, rehersail, rehersall, from rehersen and apparently partly Middle French rehercel. By surface analysis, rehearse + -al.

ex.en: With the extra rehearsals, work is really tight.
ex.ja: リハの回数増えたから仕事キチキチだよ。

ex.en: Just right now, I'm doing a rehearsal for the concert.
ex.ja: ちょうど今、コンサートのリハーサルをしています。

ex.en: After a ten-minute break, we resumed our rehearsal.
ex.ja: １０分休憩してからまたリハーサルを続けました。

note.ja: rehearse（下稽古する）+ -al。古フランス語 rehercier（再び耕す）、herse（まぐわ）。「何度も繰り返すこと」→「リハーサル」。hearse（霊柩車）も同じ herse。

en: To strengthen, especially by addition or augmentation.
To emphasize or review.

English inforce
English reinforce
From re- + inforce.

note.ja: re（再び）+ inforce（強くする）。force（力）。「再び力を加える」→「強化する」。

en: The act of starting something again.
To start again.
Synonym of reboot.

restart.ety:

ex.ja: PCを再起動する必要があります。

ex.en: You need to restart your computer.
ex.ja: PCを再起動する必要があります。

ex.en: Please restart your computer.
ex.ja: コンピューターを再起動してください。

note.ja: re（再び）+ start（始める）。「再開する・再起動する」。

en: To cause (a person or animal) to recover from a faint; to cause (a person or animal) to return to a state of consciousness.
To bring (a person or animal which is dead) back to life.

revive.ety: The verb is derived from Late Middle English reviven, revyven (“to recover from illness; to regain consciousness; to return to life after death; to happen again, recur; to be rejuvenated, renewed; (figurative) to bring back; (alchemy) of a metal: to be restored to its original form”), from Anglo-Norman reviver, revivre (“to return to life after death; to rejuvenate, renew; to make (a law or legal document) valid again”), Middle French revivre, and Old French revivre (“to return to life after death; to rejuvenate, renew”) (modern French revivre), and directly from their etymon Latin revīvere, t

ex.en: That rose will revive if you water it.
ex.ja: 水をやればそのバラは生き返るでしょう。

ex.en: The plants will revive after a good rain.
ex.ja: 慈雨があれば草木は生き返るでしょう。

ex.en: I was revived by a glass of water.
ex.ja: 私は一杯の水で生き返った。

note.ja: re（再び）+ viv（生きる）+ e。再び生きる →「生き返らせる・復活させる」。

en: Showing, causing, or favoring rigour/rigor; scrupulously accurate or strict; thorough.
Severe; intense.

rigorous.ety: Inherited from Middle English rigorous, from Middle French and Anglo-Norman rigoreus, derived from Late Latin rigōrōsus (stiff, rigid; inflexible). By surface analysis, rigor + -ous.

ex.en: The top engineer put the car through a series of rigorous tests.
ex.ja: トップエンジニアが、その車に一連の厳重な検査を加えた。

note.ja: ラテン語 rigor（硬さ）から。硬く厳しい →「厳格な・厳密な」。

en: A long, often knitted, garment worn around the neck.
A headscarf.
To throw on loosely; to put on like a scarf.
To dress with a scarf, or as with a scarf; to cover with a loose wrapping.

scarf.ety: Probably from Old Northern French escarpe (compare Old French escharpe (“pilgrim's purse suspended from the neck”), which see). The verb is derived from the noun. Doublet of scrip.

ex.en: The girl has a scarf around her neck.
ex.ja: その女の子は首のまわりにスカーフを巻いている。

ex.en: She has a scarf around her neck.
ex.ja: 彼女は首にスカーフをまいている。

ex.en: Put your scarf on. It's cold out.
ex.ja: マフラーをしなさい。外は寒いわ。

note.ja: 古北フランス語 escarpe（肩掛けかばん）から。「スカーフ」。

en: View, natural features, landscape.
Stage backdrops, property and other items on a stage that give the impression of the location of the scene.

scenery.ety: Earlier scenary, from scene + -ary, but now remodelled as scene + -ery.

ex.en: The beauty of the scenery is beyond description.
ex.ja: その景色の美しさは筆舌に尽くしがたい。

ex.en: He was excited to see the beautiful scenery.
ex.ja: 彼はその美しい光景を見てわくわくした。

ex.en: This district is known for its beautiful scenery.
ex.ja: この地方は美しい風景で知られている。

note.ja: scene（場面）+ -ery。ギリシャ語 skēnē（テント・舞台）。「舞台の背景」→「景色」。

Conveying nerve impulses from the sense organs to the nerve centers.

en: A paved footpath located at the side of a road, for the use of pedestrians.
Any paved footpath, even if not located at the side of a road.

en: Tired; feeling the need for sleep.
Suggesting tiredness.
The gum that builds up in the eye; sleep, gound.

ex.en: I'm sleepy. Can you read me a story?
ex.ja: 眠い。本読んで。

ex.en: I'm so sleepy I'm about to fall over.
ex.ja: 眠すぎて倒れそう。

ex.en: I'm sleepy. I'm going to sleep. Good night.
ex.ja: 眠くなった。寝る。ぐない。

en: In a smooth manner; smooth.

smoothly.ety: From Middle English smoþely; equivalent to smooth + -ly.

ex.en: Their married life did not run smoothly.
ex.ja: 彼らの結婚生活はうまくいかなかった。

ex.en: Well it will probably go smoothly.
ex.ja: 多分うまく行くさ。

ex.en: I think communication is what makes an organization run smoothly.
ex.ja: コミュニケーションは組織の潤滑油だと思います。

en: A town containing merchants who have exclusive right, under royal authority, to purchase or produce certain goods for export; also, the b…
Place of supply; source.
To sort according to its staple.
Relating to, or being market of staple for, commodities.
Established in commerce; occupying the markets; settled.

ex.en: Coffee is one of the staples of Brazil.
ex.ja: コーヒーはブラジルの主要産物の一つである。

ex.en: How do you load staples into a stapler?
ex.ja: ホチキスの針って、どうやって入れればいいの？

ex.en: How do I put staples into a stapler?
ex.ja: ホチキスの針って、どうやって入れればいいの？

note.ja: 「主要産物」は古フランス語 estaple（市場）から。「ホチキスの針」は古英語 stapol（柱）からで別語とされる。

en: A conventional, formulaic, and often oversimplified or exaggerated conception, opinion, or image of (a person or a group of people).
A person who is regarded as embodying or conforming to a set image or type.
To make a stereotype of someone or something, or characterize someone by a stereotype.
To prepare for printing in stereotype; to produce stereotype plates of.

ex.ja: この番組はマンネリになっている。

ex.en: The movie is a stereotyped sob story.
ex.ja: その映画はお涙頂戴ものだ。

ex.en: The people around were stunned.
ex.ja: 周りの人は呆然としていた。

ex.en: They were stunned after finding out about his resignation.
ex.ja: 彼の辞任を知って、彼らは呆然とした。

ex.en: Grandmother died, leaving the whole family stunned.
ex.ja: おばあちゃんが突然死んで家族一同驚いた。

en: A Japanese dish made of small portions of sticky white rice flavored with vinegar, usually wrapped in seaweed and filled or topped with f…
Raw fish, especially as a Japanese dish.
To prepare (a food) as sushi.

sushi.ety: Borrowed from Japanese 寿司(すし) (sushi, “sushi (sour rice)”), ultimately from archaic conjugation 酸(す)し (sushi, “sour, vinegared”) of modern adjective 酸(す)い (sui, “sour, vinegared”).

ex.ja: 今夜、寿司を食べに行きませんか。

ex.en: How about going to a sushi bar right now?
ex.ja: 今すぐ、すし屋さんに行くなんてどうですか。

note.ja: 日本語「寿司」から。

en: The state of being swollen.
Anything swollen, especially any abnormally swollen part of the body.

ex.en: You may have swelling, but don't worry about it.
ex.ja: 腫れるかもしれませんが気にしないでください。

ex.en: How many days will it take until the swelling goes down?
ex.ja: 腫れが引くまで何日くらいかかりますか。

ex.en: His knee turned a ghastly blackish purple from the swelling.
ex.ja: 彼の膝は腫れてぞっとするような黒紫色になってしまった。

note.ja: swell（膨らむ）+ -ing。「腫れ・膨張」。

en: A treatise on terms, especially those used in a specialised field.
The set of terms actually used in any business, art, science, or the like; nomenclature; technical terms.

terminology.ety: From French terminologie or German Terminologie and their source, New Latin terminologia, from Medieval Latin terminus (“a term”) + -ologia (“study of”), from -o- (“(interconsonantal)”) + -logia, from Ancient Greek -λογία (-logía, “-logy, branch of study, to speak”).

note.ja: termin（境界・用語）+ o + log（言葉）+ y。用語の体系 →「専門用語・術語」。

en: Of or relating to the theatre.
Fake and exaggerated.
A stage performance, especially one by amateurs.
A commercially produced film to be shown in movie theaters.

theatrical.ety: From Latin theātricus + -al. By surface analysis, theatre + -ical.

ex.en: His behavior was theatrical.
ex.ja: 彼の振る舞いは芝居じみていた。

Someone who lives (particularly in the UK) in a caravan, bus or other vehicle rather than a fixed abode.

traveller.ety: From Middle English traveler, travelour, travailere, travailour (“worker", also "traveller”), equivalent to travel + -er. Compare Anglo-Norman travailur, travailour, Old French travailleor, travelleeur, travelier.

Sharing the same views or opinions, and being in harmony or accord.

Desire for revenge.

Proto-Italic *n̥-

ex.en: The man charged me with being irresponsible.
ex.ja: その男は私を無責任だと非難した。

ex.ja: 約束を破るとは彼も無責任だ。

ex.ja: 約束を破るなんて無責任だ。

en: Late.
Last made; hence, made of refuse; inferior.
A gap, a delay; an interval created by something not keeping up; a latency.
Delay; latency.
To fail to keep up (the pace), to fall behind.
To cover (for example, pipes) with felt strips or similar material.

lag.ety: Of unknown origin. Possibly of North Germanic origin.

ex.en: He lags behind in science.
ex.ja: 彼は理科で後れをとっている。

ex.en: He's lagging behind in science.
ex.ja: 彼は理科で後れをとっている。

ex.en: I've got a bad case of jet lag.
ex.ja: 時差ボケで辛い。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。「遅れる」。jet lag（時差ぼけ）。

en: One who lends, especially money; specifically, a bank or other entity that specializes in granting loans.

lender.ety: From Middle English lendare, leendare, variants of lenner, lenere, equivalent to lend + -er.

ex.en: That man borrows money from many lenders.
ex.ja: あの男の人は多重債務者である。

ex.en: Money lenders are enjoying a profitable period.
ex.ja: 資金の貸し手は高利益の時期を享受している。

en: The fact or quality of having a position in space.
The features or surroundings of a particular place.

locality.ety: From French localité, from Late Latin localitas, equivalent to local + -ity.

ex.en: The locality does not count for much in Japan.
ex.ja: 日本では土地勘というものは、あまり価値がない。

ex.en: Localities imposed bans on development.
ex.ja: いくつかの地方自治体では開発を禁止した。

en: Something that tempts or attracts, especially one with a promise of reward or pleasure.
An artificial bait attached to a fishing line to attract fish.
To attract by temptation, appeal, or guile.
To attract fish with a lure.

lure.ety: From Anglo-Norman lure, from Old French loirre (Modern French leurre), from Frankish *lōþr, from Proto-Germanic *lōþr-, perhaps ultimately related to *laþō (“invitation, calling”), or from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂- (“to hide”). Compare English allure, also from Old French. Probably related to German Luder (“bait”).

ex.en: The dress lured her into the store.
ex.ja: そのドレスにひかれて彼女はその店の中に入った。

ex.en: He lured her away from her husband.
ex.ja: 彼女を夫の手からおびき出した。

ex.en: He felt the lure of adventure.
ex.ja: 彼は冒険の誘惑を感じた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 loirre（鷹を呼び戻すおとり）から。「誘い込む・疑似餌」。

en: Intending to do harm; characterized by spite and malice.

malicious.ety: From Middle English malicious, from Old French malicios, from Latin malitiōsus, from malitia (“malice”), from malus (“bad”). Displaced native Middle English ivelwilled and ivelwilly (“malicious”), related to Old English yfelwillende (literally “evil-willing”). By surface analysis, malice + -ious.

ex.en: Please tell me how to deal with malicious comments.
ex.ja: 陰湿な嫌がらせを受けた場合の対処法について教えてください。

ex.en: Beware of 'One Ring' malicious nuisance calls!!
ex.ja: 悪質な迷惑電話、ワンギリにご注意！！

note.ja: ラテン語 malitia（悪意）から。malus（悪い）。「悪意のある」。malice、malware と同じ mal。

To cover with a thick layer, like a mattress; to blanket.

ex.en: Do you really hide your money under the mattress?
ex.ja: 本当にマットレスの下にお金隠してるの？

ex.en: I need a new mattress.
ex.ja: 新しいマットレスがいるな。

ex.en: I hid it under the mattress.
ex.ja: マットレスの下に隠しました。

note.ja: アラビア語 maṭraḥ（敷物・クッション）から、イタリア語を経た語。

en: A naevus, a pigmented, slightly raised, and sometimes hairy spot on the skin.
To create a network of channels in (waterlogged soil) to improve drainage.

mole.ety:
From Middle English mole, mool, from Old English māl (“a mole, spot, mark, blemish”), from Proto-West Germanic *mail, from Proto-Germanic *mailą (“spot, wrinkle”), from Proto-Indo-European *mel-, *melw- (“dark, dirty”), from Proto-Indo-European *mey-, *my- (“to soil, sully”).
Cognate with Scots mail (“spot, stain”), Saterland Frisian Moal (“scar”), German dialectal Meil (“spot, stain, blemish”), Gothic 𐌼𐌰𐌹𐌻 (mail, “spot, blemish”).

ex.en: Mary has a mole under her eye.
ex.ja: メアリーには泣きぼくろがある。

ex.en: That person has a mole at the side of his eye.
ex.ja: あの人は眼の横にほくろがある。

ex.en: I don't think people should make a mountain of a mole hill.
ex.ja: 針ほどのことを棒ほどにいうのはどうかと思います。

note.ja: 「ほくろ」は古英語 māl、「モグラ」は中英語 molle からで別語。モグラのように潜り込む →「スパイ」。

en: A government in which sovereignty is embodied within a single, today usually hereditary head of state (whether as a figurehead or as a po…
The territory ruled over by a monarch; a kingdom.

monarchy.ety: From Old French monarchie, from Late Latin monarchia, from Ancient Greek μοναρχία (monarkhía), from μόνος (mónos, “only”) + ἀρχή (arkhḗ, “power, authority”). By surface analysis, mon- (“one, single”) + -archy (“rule, command”).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 monos（ひとりの）+ archein（治める）。「ひとりが治めること」→「君主制」。monarch。

en: Of, relating to, or connected with muscles.
Brawny, thewy, having strength.

muscular.ety: Late 17th century; from muscle (Latin mūsculus) + -ar. Compare French musculaire.

ex.en: With his muscular constitution he passes for a judoist.
ex.ja: 骨格たくましい体格なので彼は柔道家でとおっている。

ex.en: My muscular strength has weakened from lack of exercise.
ex.ja: 運動不足で筋肉が弱くなった。

ex.en: The bullet penetrated his muscular chest.
ex.ja: 弾丸は彼の厚い胸板を貫通した。

note.ja: muscle（筋肉）+ -ar。ラテン語 musculus（小さなネズミ）。力こぶの動きがネズミに見えたことから。

en: The state or quality of being neutral; the condition of being unengaged in contests between others; state of taking no part on either side.
The quality or state of being neutral.

neutrality.ety: From Middle French neutralité, from Medieval Latin neutralitas. Morphologically neutral + -ity.

ex.en: The alternative possibilities are neutrality or war.
ex.ja: 可能性は中立か戦争かの二つに一つだ。

ex.ja: 外に行こう。ここは騒がしすぎるよ。

ex.ja: その通りは昼間は大変騒がしかった。

ex.ja: パンツが大嫌いです。

ex.ja: 店員さんがそう言うなら、ブラジャーとパンティーも買ってってやろう。

en: A package wrapped, as for shipment or transport.
An individual consignment of cargo for shipment, regardless of size and form.
To wrap something up into the form of a package.
To wrap a strip around the end of a rope.

parcel.ety: From Middle English parcel, from Old French parcelle (“a small piece or part, a parcel, a particle”), from Late Latin particella, diminutive of Latin particula (“particle”), diminutive of partem (“part, piece”). Doublet of particle.

ex.ja: この小包を郵便局へ持って行ってください。

ex.ja: この小包をすぐ送りたい。

ex.ja: 日本に小包を送りたいのですが。

en: An action which divides a thing into parts, or separates one thing from another.
A part of something that has been divided.
To divide something into parts, sections or shares.
To divide a region or country into two or more territories with separate political status.

partition.ety: Recorded c.1430, "division into shares, distinction," from Middle English particioun, from Old French particion (modern partition), from Latin partitio, partitionem (“division, portion”), from partitus, the past participle of partire (“to split (up), part(ition)”).

ex.en: Can a body, hand, or finger enter the safety partition?
ex.ja: 安全用パーテーションに体・手・指が入れるか？

ex.en: The hall could seat a thousand people before it was partitioned.
ex.ja: ホールは仕切りを設ける前は千人収容できた。

ex.ja: 弾丸は仕切り壁を貫いた。

note.ja: part（分ける）+ ition。分けること →「仕切り・分割（する）」。

en: Out of the ordinary; odd; strange; unusual.
Common or usual for a certain place or circumstance; specific or particular.
That which is peculiar; a sole or exclusive property; a prerogative; a characteristic.
an ecclesiastical district, parish, chapel or church outside the jurisdiction of the bishop of the diocese in which it is situated.

peculiar.ety: From Latin pecūliāris (“one's own”), from pecūlium (“private property”), from pecus (“cattle”).

ex.en: Can you name any plants peculiar to Japan?
ex.ja: 日本にしかない植物の名を幾つか挙げられますか。

ex.en: The odd custom is peculiar to the region.
ex.ja: その変わった習慣はその地方特有のものだ。

ex.en: This style of cooking is peculiar to China.
ex.ja: この調理法は中国独特のものだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 peculium（自分の財産）から。pecu（家畜）。「自分だけの」→「独特の・変な」。

en: Of or relating to property or ownership.
Owning something; having ownership.
A proprietor or owner.
A body of proprietors, taken collectively.

proprietary.ety: From French propriétaire, from Latin proprietārius. By surface analysis, propriety + -ary. Compare with the Latin proprietas (“property”) and proprius (“ownership”).

To disseminate one's own opinions in a—typically—one-sided, strong manner.
A criticism done by ranting.
A wild, emotional, and sometimes incoherent articulation.

An irregular distribution or sprinkling of objects resembling a rash (sense 1).

A copy made at a smaller scale than the original.

replica.ety: Borrowed from Italian replica, derived from Latin replicare (“to fold or bend back; to reply”). Doublet of reply and replicate.

note.ja: イタリア語 replica（繰り返し）から。re（再び）+ plic（折る）。折り返して作ったもの →「複製・レプリカ」。reply（返事）も同じ。

en: To dwell permanently or for a considerable time; to have a settled abode for a time; to remain for a long time.
To have a seat or fixed position; to inhere; to lie or be as in attribute or element.

reside.ety: From Middle English residen, from Old French resider, from Latin resideō (“remain behind, reside, dwell”), from re- (“back”) + sedeō (“sit”).

ex.en: Is Japan a good place to reside?
ex.ja: 日本って、住み心地がいい？

ex.en: Is Japan a pleasant place to reside?
ex.ja: 日本って、住み心地がいい？

ex.en: Let happiness reside within all living beings.
ex.ja: 生きとし生けるものが幸せでありますように。

Of a food, advanced to the state of fitness for use; mellow.
A fruit or vegetable which has ripened.
To ripen or mature.

ex.ja: この果物は摘み取られるほどのは成長していない。

ex.ja: そのりんごはまだ完全に熟してはない。

ex.en: He lived to a ripe old age.
ex.ja: 彼は天寿を全うした。

A child who is conceived in order to provide an organ or cell transplant to a sibling who has an otherwise fatal disease (used in combina…

en: having beautiful scenery; picturesque
of or relating to scenery
A depiction of scenery.
A scenic artist; a person employed to design backgrounds for theatre etc.

en: A small mouthful of drink.
An event at which people drink alcohol in small, usually subintoxicating amounts.
To drink slowly, small mouthfuls at a time.
To drink a small quantity.

ex.en: May I have a sip of your coffee?
ex.ja: コーヒー、一口いただいてもいいかしら？

ex.en: Give me a sip of that.
ex.ja: それ一口ちょうだい。

ex.en: He sipped the hot coffee slowly.
ex.ja: 彼は熱いコーヒーをゆっくりすすった。

en: Any of very many animals (either hermaphroditic or nonhermaphroditic), of the class Gastropoda, having a coiled shell.

To move or travel very slowly.

ex.ja: 「でんでん虫って、なんてデカいんだ」と、てんとう虫は言いました。

ex.ja: カタツムリって好き？

ex.ja: ボブはカタツムリを食べて、その後吐いた。

To arouse an organism to functional activity.

ex.ja: 金利が低下したことが自動車の市場を刺激した。

ex.ja: この政策は、景気を刺激するのにきっと大いに役立つであろう。

ex.ja: ほめることが学習者にやる気を起こさせる。

note.ja: ラテン語 stimulare（突き棒で突く）から。「刺激する」。stimulus と同じ。

en: In a strange or coincidental manner.

strangely.ety: From Middle English straungely (“strangely, aloofly, intricately”); equivalent to strange + -ly.

ex.en: Strangely enough, I felt no pain at all.
ex.ja: 不思議なことに、全く痛みを感じなかった。

ex.en: Strangely enough, I didn't feel any pain at all.
ex.ja: 妙な話だが、私は何の痛みも感じなかった。

ex.en: They're strangely close for two guys, don't you think?
ex.ja: 男同士にしては変に仲がいいね。

en: Likely to be affected by something.
Easily influenced or tricked; credulous.
A person who is vulnerable to being infected by a certain disease

susceptible.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin susceptibilis, from Latin susceptus, from suscipiō.

ex.en: They are susceptible to changes in fashion.
ex.ja: 彼らは流行に敏感だ。

ex.en: Elderly people are more susceptible to illness.
ex.ja: 高齢者は病気になりやすい。

ex.en: She was susceptible to colds.
ex.ja: 彼女は風邪を引きやすかった。

note.ja: sus（下から）+ cept（取る）+ ible。下から受け取りやすい →「影響を受けやすい・（病気に）かかりやすい」。

en: A person or thing that translates various forms of text.
Synonym of interpreter, a person or thing that immediately interprets direct speech.

translator.ety: Directly from Latin trānslātor and French translator, and also from Middle English translatour, from Old French translatour, translateur, etc., from Latin trānslātor, from trānslātus (“carried across”) + -or (“-er: forming agent nouns”), from trānsferō (“carry across”), from trans (“across”) + ferō (“bear, carry”), q.v. Equivalent to translate + -or.

ex.en: Because I want to be a translator.
ex.ja: なぜなら私は翻訳家になりたいからです。

ex.en: The translator found it impossible to explain what he meant.
ex.ja: 翻訳者は、彼の言っていることを説明するのは不可能だとわかった。

ex.en: I don't like using Google Translator.
ex.ja: Google翻訳を使うのは嫌だな。

note.ja: trans（向こうへ）+ lat（運ばれた）+ or。向こうへ運ぶ人 →「翻訳者」。

en: To send or convey from one person, place or thing to another.
To spread or pass on (something such as a disease or a signal).

transmit.ety: From Middle English transmitten, borrowed from Latin trānsmittō (“transmit”, verb, literally “across-send”).

ex.en: His will was transmitted to his younger brother.
ex.ja: 彼の意志は弟に伝えられた。

ex.en: The Vice-President transmitted the message by radio.
ex.ja: 副大統領はメッセージをラジオで伝えた。

ex.en: He has transmitted all his knowledge to his son.
ex.ja: 彼は息子にすべての知識を伝えた。

note.ja: trans（向こうへ）+ mit（送る）。向こうへ送る →「送信する・伝える・感染させる」。

en: One who teaches another (usually called a student, learner, or tutee) in a one-on-one or small-group interaction.
A university officer responsible for students in a particular hall.
To instruct or teach, especially an individual or small group.

tutor.ety: From Middle English tutour, from Old French tuteur (French tuteur), from Latin tūtor (“a watcher, protector, guardian”), from tueor (“protect”); see tuition.

ex.en: I found a tutor through a newspaper ad.
ex.ja: 新聞の広告で、家庭教師を見つけました。

ex.en: My tutor scolded me for my stupid behavior.
ex.ja: 家庭教師の先生は私が馬鹿なことをしたと叱った。

ex.en: Even my tutor couldn't solve this equation.
ex.ja: 私のチューターでさえこの方程式は解けなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 tutor（保護者）から。tueri（見守る）。「家庭教師」。tuition と同じ。

en: A rod or staff of office, e.g. of a verger.
The stick or wand with which persons were formerly admitted tenants, by holding it in the hand and swearing fealty to the lord. Such tena…
To be or come very close; to border; to approach.
To bend or incline; to tend downward; to slope.

verge.ety: Borrowed from Middle French verge (“rod or wand of office”), hence "scope, territory dominated", from Latin virga (“shoot, rod stick”), of unknown origin. Earliest attested sense in English is now-obsolete meaning "male member, penis" (c.1400). Modern sense is from the notion of 'within the verge' (1509, also as Anglo-Norman dedeinz la verge), i.e. "subject to the Lord High Steward's authority" (as symbolized by the rod of office), originally a 12-mile radius round the royal court, which sense shifted to "the outermost edge of an expanse or area." Doublet of virga.

ex.en: The world is on the verge of destruction.
ex.ja: 世界は破滅の淵に立たされている。

ex.en: She was on the verge of killing herself.
ex.ja: 彼女は自殺寸前だった。

ex.en: Tom is on the verge of crying.
ex.ja: トムは今にも泣きそうです。

note.ja: ラテン語 virga（棒・枝）から。「境界を示す棒」→「縁・瀬戸際」。

en: Pulsing with energy or activity.
Lively and vigorous.
Any of a class of consonants including taps and trills.

vibrant.ety: From French vibrant, from Latin vibrans, present participle of vibrare (“to vibrate”). See vibrate.

ex.en: While taking a walk, Tom enjoyed the autumn leaves in vibrant red and orange.
ex.ja: 散歩をしながら、トムは鮮やかな赤とオレンジ色の紅葉を堪能しました。

note.ja: ラテン語 vibrare（振動させる）から。「震えるような」→「活気に満ちた・鮮やかな」。vibe、vibration と同じ。

en: An often humid, yellowish froth produced by fermenting malt worts, and used to brew beer, leaven bread, and also used in certain medicines.

To ferment.
To rise.

yeast.ety: From Middle English yest, yeest, gest, gist, from Old English ġist, ġyst, from Proto-West Germanic *jestu, from Proto-Germanic *jestuz. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Jääst (“yeast”), West Frisian gêst, gist (“yeast”), Dutch gist (“yeast”), German Low German Gest (“yeast”), German Gischt (“sea foam”), Swedish jäst (“yeast”), Norwegian jest (“yeast”), Icelandic jöstur (“yeast”).

ex.en: Yeast acts as an agent in making bread rise.
ex.ja: イースト菌はパンを膨らませる際の作用剤だ。

ex.en: Bread is made from flour, water and yeast.
ex.ja: パンは粉と水とイーストから作られる。

ex.en: Bread is made from flour, water, and often yeast.
ex.ja: パンは小麦粉と水と、それにしばしばイーストを加えてから作られる。

note.ja: 古英語 gist から。「泡立つもの」が原義。

en: Someone who intentionally kills a person, especially a professional who kills a public or political figure.
Any ruthless killer.

assassin.ety:
From either French assassin or Italian assassino, from Arabic أَسَاسِيِّين (ʔasāsiyyīn, “people who are faithful to the foundation [of the faith]”) and the folkloric etymology Arabic حَشَّاشِين (ḥaššāšīn, “hashish users; low-lives”).
The mathematical sense was introduced by Bourbaki, playing on the notation operatorname Ass(M) and the fact that an associated prime is the annihilator of an element, and so is said to kill that element.

note.ja: アラビア語 ḥashshāshīn（大麻を使う者）から。中世の暗殺教団の呼び名。assassination と同じ。

en: A suddenly reversed or backward motion, such as of a rope or elastic band when it snaps under tension.
A negative reaction, objection or outcry, especially of a violent or abrupt nature.
To perform a backlash, to lash back in reaction to some cause.

ex.en: The bribery scandal created a backlash overseas.
ex.ja: 収賄スキャンダルは海外で激しい反発を生みました。

note.ja: back（後ろへ）+ lash（むち打ち）。機械のがたつき・跳ね返り →「反発・反動」。

en: A shared record of past transactions in a distributed network, typically used for cryptocurrency.

blockchain.ety: From block + chain, from earlier “block chain”. In the 2008 Bitcoin paper block and chain are used separately; the concept is referred to as “chain of hash-based proof-of-work” or “chain of digital signatures”.

note.ja: block（塊）+ chain（鎖）。「データのブロックを鎖のようにつないだもの」。

en: A building where beer is produced.
A company that brews beer.

note.ja: brew（醸造する）+ -ery（場所）。「醸造所」。

To take the shape of a bulb; to swell.

ex.ja: 小さな裸電球が唯一の明りだった。

ex.ja: 電球が切れた。

ex.en: Thomas Edison invented the light bulb.
ex.ja: トマス・エジソンが電球を発明した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 bolbos（タマネギ・球根）から。「球根」→ 球根の形 →「電球」。

Something flat or insubstantial.

Flat or flavorless.

ex.ja: 荷物をまとめるために、段ボールの箱が欲しいんです。

en: In a casual manner.

casually.ety: From Middle English casually, casuelly, casuali, casuely, equivalent to casual + -ly.

ex.ja: この話し方が好きじゃなければ、カジュアルに話してくれていいよ。

ex.en: He picked up the newspaper and glanced casually over the front page.
ex.ja: 彼は新聞を取り上げて何気なく１面を眺めた。

en: To crush with the teeth by repeated closing and opening of the jaws; done to food to soften it and break it down by the action of saliva …
To grind, tear, or otherwise degrade or demolish something with teeth or as with teeth.
The act of chewing; mastication with the mouth.
Level of chewiness.

chew.ety: From Middle English chewen, from Old English ċēowan, from Proto-West Germanic *keuwan, from Proto-Germanic *kewwaną, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵyewh₁-. Cognate with West Frisian kôgje, Low German käwwen, Dutch kauwen, German kauen; also Latin gingīva (“gums”), Tocharian B śuwaṃ (“to eat”), Polish żuć (“to chew”), Persian جویدن (javidan), Pashto ژُوَل (žovạl, “to bite, gnaw”).

A security or guarantee (usually an asset) pledged for the repayment of a loan if one cannot procure enough funds to repay.
A branch of a bodily part or system of organs.

Blocking up of the capillary and other blood vessels, etc., in any locality or organ (often producing other morbid symptoms); local hyper…

ex.en: We know how to get around traffic congestion.
ex.ja: 私たちは交通渋滞をうまく避ける方法を知っている。

ex.en: Our delay was due to traffic congestion.
ex.ja: 私たちが遅れたのは交通が混雑していたからです。

ex.en: In spite of the terrible congestion, I was in time for the appointment.
ex.ja: ひどい渋滞にもかかわらず、私は定刻に間に合った。

en: A person to whom a debt is owed.
One who gives credence to something; a believer.

creditor.ety: From Middle English creditour, from Anglo-Norman creditour, from Latin crēditor, from crēditum (“loan”), from crēditus, perfect passive participle of crēdō (“lend”).

The means by which a crossing is made.
Of an electrical cable, having connector pins at one end wired to different pins at the other; for example, pin 1 to pin 2, pin 2 to pin …
Configured so that the transmit signals at one end are connected to the receive signals at the other.

Happening during the day.

To convey, as by will or lease.
To transmit by inheritance.

An irresistible physical or psychological need, especially for a chemical substance.

ex.en: I'm in dire need of money.
ex.ja: どうしてもお金が必要なんだ。

A condition of not agreeing or concurring.

ex.en: Jim sometimes has disagreements with his wife.
ex.ja: ジムさんは時々、妻といさかいをする。

ex.en: The chairman did not rule out the possibility of a disagreement.
ex.ja: 議長は意見が不一致に終る可能性を排除しなかった。

ex.ja: 大きな意見の不一致があることが時々ある。

en: A person who learns from another, especially one who then teaches others.
An active follower or adherent of someone, or some philosophy etc.
To convert (a person) into a disciple.
To train, educate, teach.

ex.ja: しかし、使徒たちはその危険に気付いた。

ex.ja: その翌日。またヨハネは、二人の弟子と共に立っていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 discipulus（生徒）から。discere（学ぶ）。「弟子」。discipline（教え・規律）と同じ。

en: The act or state of deliberately not paying attention or caring about something.
To ignore; to pay no attention to.

ex.en: He has a disregard for the law.
ex.ja: 彼は法律を構わず無視する。

ex.en: She continued to see him in disregard of my advice.
ex.ja: 彼女は私の忠告を無視して彼との交際を続けた。

ex.en: Sorry. I said too much. Disregard what I just said.
ex.ja: ごめん。言い過ぎた。今、私が言ったことは、気にしないで。

note.ja: dis（否定）+ regard（注意を払う）。「無視する」。

Predominance; ascendancy.

dominion.ety: From Middle English dominion, from Middle French dominion, from Latin dominium (“lordship, right of ownership”), from dominus (“lord”), from domus (“house”). See demain, demesne, domain, dominium.

ex.ja: 人間は鳥や動物を支配しているだろうか。

So as to deteriorate or get worse.
Located towards or at the bottom of a slope or hill.
Going down a slope or a hill.
The fastest of the disciplines of alpine skiing.
A rapid descent of a hill in related sports, especially in alpine skiing.
To take part in downhill skiing.

ex.en: For a girl, after 30, it's downhill all the way.
ex.ja: 女は３０を過ぎてからはずっと下り坂だ。

ex.ja: 午後から天気は下り坂になります。

note.ja: down（下へ）+ hill（丘）。「坂を下って」→「悪化して」。

en: Genuinely horrific, awful, or alarming; dangerous, risky.
Unpleasant, awful, very bad (also used as an intensifier).
Dreadfully.
A shocker: a report of a crime written in a provokingly lurid style.
A journal or broadsheet printing such reports.

dreadful.ety: From Middle English dredful, dredfull, dredeful (also dreful). By surface analysis, dread + -ful.

ex.en: I had a feeling that something dreadful was happening.
ex.ja: 何か恐ろしいことが起こりそうな気がした。

ex.en: A dreadful accident happened on the corner.
ex.ja: 町角で恐ろしい事故が起きた。

ex.en: I had a dreadful dream last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜恐ろしい夢を見ました。

note.ja: dread（恐れ）+ -ful。「恐ろしい」→「ひどい」。

en: To remove (markings or information).
To obliterate information from (a storage medium), such as to clear or (with magnetic storage) to demagnetize.
The operation of deleting data.

ex.ja: 私は彼女が涙を流した思い出を忘れようと努めた。

en: Having had population removed, by evacuation.
Containing a vacuum.

ex.en: The people were evacuated because of the flood.
ex.ja: 大水のため人々は立ち退いた。

en: Of feelings, a person's spirit, a state of affairs, etc.: put out, as if like a fire; quenched, suppressed.
Of customs, ideas, laws and legal rights, offices, organizations, languages, etc.: no longer existing or in use; defunct, discontinued, o…

extinct.ety: From Late Middle English extinct (“eliminated, eradicated, extinguished”), from Latin extīnctus, exstīnctus (“extinguished, quenched; destroyed, killed; made extinct”), the perfect passive participles of extinguō, exstinguō (“to extinguish, put out, quench; (figurative) to abolish; to destroy, kill”), from ex- (prefix meaning ‘away; out’) + stinguō (“to extinguish, put out, quench”) (from Proto-Indo-European *stengʷ- (“to push”)). The Middle English word displaced Middle English aqueint, aquenched (“extinct; extinguished”). Doublet of extinguish.

ex.en: This custom became extinct a long time ago.
ex.ja: この習慣は絶えて久しい。

ex.en: Dinosaurs became extinct a very long time ago.
ex.ja: 恐竜は大昔に絶滅した。

ex.en: Unless whales are protected, they will become extinct.
ex.ja: 鯨は保護されなければ、絶滅するだろう。

note.ja: ラテン語 exstinctus（消された）から。「（火が）消えた」→「絶滅した」。extinction と同じ。

en: To disallow; to proscribe.
To deny, exclude from, or warn off, by express command.

forbid.ety:

Norwegian Bokmål forby (“to forbid”), Swedish förbjuda (“to forbid”), Gothic 𐍆𐌰𐌿𐍂𐌱𐌹𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌽 (faurbiudan). Related to forbode.

ex.ja: 両親は私がまたトムと会うことを禁止した。

ex.en: My father forbids me to go out at night.
ex.ja: 父は私が夜外出するのを禁止している。

ex.en: I forbid smoking in my room.
ex.ja: 私の部屋での喫煙を禁ずる。

note.ja: for（反対に）+ bid（命じる）。「しないように命じる」→「禁じる」。forbidden。

en: In a manner relating to genes or genetics.
In terms of origin or development.

The meat from this animal.
To move swiftly.
Grey, hoary; grey-haired, venerable (of people).
Cold, frosty (of weather).

ex.ja: 二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず。

ex.en: First, catch your hare, then cook him.
ex.ja: まず現物を手に入れよ。

Voluntary.
A person who holds an honorary appointment.
A kind of secret society that operates in name only, with membership given to honor some achievement.

ex.ja: 大学は彼に名誉学位を与えた。

ex.ja: フランクス陸軍大将がナイト爵位の名誉称号を授かりました。

Childish in behavior; juvenile.
An immature member of a species.

Having qualities viewed as befitting a man; masculine, manful, courageous, resolute, noble.
In a way befitting a man.

ex.ja: トムはあまり男らしくない。

ex.ja: 他人の悪口をかげで言うのは男らしくない。

en: The state of being a mother; motherhood.
The state of being pregnant; pregnancy.

maternity.ety: From French maternité, from Latin māternitās.

ex.ja: 彼女は来週から産休に入る。

ex.en: I'll be on maternity leave from 30 September to 14 October.
ex.ja: ９月３０日から１０月１４日まで産休を取ります。

ex.en: After her maternity leave, she resumed her old job.
ex.ja: 産休のあと彼女はまたもとの仕事に戻った。
